Definition: from G91; a wrong done:--evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong.
BiblicalUsage: Adikema is a wrong done — a specific act of injustice rather than wrongness in general. Gallio uses it when the Jews accuse Paul, asking whether he has done any 'matter of wrong'; Paul uses it before Felix, challenging his accusers to name his 'evil doing'; and Revelation uses it of Babylon, whose iniquities God has remembered. The word always points at something done, something that can be named and judged.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word keeps judgment honest. God does not judge vague badness; He judges deeds — real wrongs, done by real people, with real victims — and the same word that accuses Babylon also promises that every wrong will be answered.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
